greeting: Good morning, Zuhair. Here's your Wednesday round-up, with a slightly lighter computer science shelf today.

lead.headline: Early voting opens across Victoria as the leaders' debate goes badly for Premier Carroll
lead.summary: Early voting centres opened today ahead of the 28 November state election, with more than half of voters expected to cast ballots early. The sole leaders' debate was judged a clear win for Liberal leader Jess Wilson in an audience poll, with Premier Ben Carroll trailing badly.

stories.headline: Roadmap proposes 'ecological foundation models'
stories.summary: A Perspective in Nature Machine Intelligence (6 Nov) led by Queen Mary University of London argues for AI models trained on many kinds of ecological data at once, and sets out how to integrate data, build in ecological theory and test reliability. Note: a few days older than the usual window.

stories.headline: Magnetic order shapes lattice vibrations, with implications for AI and quantum hardware
stories.summary: A UCLA study in Nature Communications (reported 12 Nov) examines how a material's magnetic order affects vibrations through its crystal lattice, with relevance to future AI and quantum computing devices.

stories.headline: Preprint: AI 'scientists' often fail to reproduce quantum research results
stories.summary: PREPRINT (not peer-reviewed, arXiv, 2 Nov): the authors find current AI scientist systems struggle to reproduce published quantum computing results and propose a self-improving system called Residual Agents.

stories.headline: OpenAI reportedly launches ChatGPT Wallet and disbands robotics team
stories.summary: A weekly AI roundup reports OpenAI is letting agents make purchases for users through ChatGPT Wallet and has wound down its robotics team, arguing general models can drive robots. It also notes chip orders from OpenAI and Anthropic extending Google TPU demand.

stories.headline: AI infrastructure scale and policy dominate Tuesday's news
stories.summary: A 17 November daily digest tracks the day's AI developments, centred on the continuing build-out of AI infrastructure and related policy moves.

stories.headline: Everything that happened in AI on Tuesday 17 November
stories.summary: The Neuron's daily digest rounds up the day's AI announcements and industry moves in one place.

stories.headline: Only leaders' debate: Jess Wilson judged the clear winner
stories.summary: An ABC analysis says the Victorian election debate was light on policy, but audience polling gave Liberal leader Jess Wilson the win while Premier Ben Carroll scored just 7 per cent.

stories.headline: Big Build royal commission begins public hearings
stories.summary: Public hearings have started in the royal commission into corruption on Victoria's Big Build projects, with an initial focus on a rail project and alleged CFMEU links to organised crime.

stories.headline: Victorians embrace pre-poll voting as the election nears
stories.summary: Early voting is becoming the norm in Victoria, with nearly half of 2022 votes cast early and the electoral commission aiming to count most first-preference votes on election night.

stories.headline: Trump, Xi and Putin eye unprecedented trilateral talks at APEC in Shenzhen
stories.summary: The APEC leaders' meeting runs 18-19 November in Shenzhen, where a first three-way meeting between the US, Chinese and Russian leaders is planned, with nuclear arms control and Iran on the agenda.

stories.headline: Morning recap: Canada and China extend trade deals, Russian military plane crash
stories.summary: Xi met Canada's Carney ahead of APEC and trade deals were extended, while a Russian military An-12 crashed in the Kemerovo region, killing all 17 aboard.

thought: The best way to predict the future is to invent it. - Alan Kay
